verdict: NRG's revenue rose 11% to $7.5B as the generation fleet it bought from LS Power lifted the East, and while GAAP profit was flattered by mark-to-market hedge gains, NRG reaffirmed its full-year guidance.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs a $0.62 loss a year ago

segments.name: Texas
segments.note: Selling power and gas to homes and businesses in Texas, plus NRG's Texas power plants. Revenue slipped 3% on milder weather and higher supply costs.

segments.name: East
segments.note: The eastern US retail business plus the generation portfolio and CPower business acquired from LS Power — the growth engine of the quarter, up 28%.

segments.name: West/Other & corporate
segments.note: Western US operations and other activities ($644M), combined here with corporate and intersegment eliminations (-$9M) so the segments add to total revenue.

segments.name: Vivint Smart Home
segments.note: Smart-home security and energy products sold by subscription — up 12%.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of power plants and customer relationships over their lives — up sharply after the LS Power acquisition added a large fleet.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling power contracts and running the company day to day — down from $724M a year ago.

opex.name: Acquisition-related costs
opex.note: Transaction and integration costs for the LS Power portfolio acquisition.

opex.name: Gain on sale of assets
opex.note: A $37M gain on selling assets — a credit inside operating costs, so it reduces expenses (shown as a negative expense, as on Duke Energy's page).

otherDetail: Other expense of $330M, net: $310M of interest expense (roughly double a year ago, after debt taken on for the LS Power deal), a $9M loss on paying off debt early, and $17M of preferred-stock dividends, partly offset by $6M of other income — so the flow lands on the $489M available to common stockholders.

takeaways.title: The LS Power deal drives the East
takeaways.text: East revenue jumped 28% to $3,512M and its adjusted EBITDA rose from $99M to $469M, thanks to the generation assets and CPower business bought from LS Power and higher capacity prices.

takeaways.title: Texas had a softer quarter
takeaways.text: Texas revenue slipped 3% and adjusted EBITDA fell to $381M from $512M, on milder weather (heating degree days down about 30% in the first half), higher supply costs and the cost of running the new plants.

takeaways.title: Full-year guidance reaffirmed
takeaways.text: NRG kept its 2026 guidance: adjusted EPS of $7.90–$9.90 and adjusted EBITDA of $5,325–$5,825M. GAAP profit of $506M was well above adjusted net income of $315M because of unrealized hedge gains (see one-time items).

oneTimers: GAAP results include unrealized mark-to-market gains on economic hedges — power contracts revalued each quarter while the customer contracts they hedge are not. That is the main reason GAAP net income of $506M was well above adjusted net income of $315M; these gains can reverse before the contracts settle.
A $37M gain on the sale of assets sits inside operating income this quarter.
footerNote: NRG had not reported Q3 2026 as of November 7, 2026, so this page covers its latest reported quarter, Q2 2026. Adaptation for a utility: cost of operations (fuel, purchased power and other direct costs) is treated as cost of revenue; the remaining operating lines mirror NRG's income statement. Segment revenue is GAAP revenue by segment from the Form 10-Q. Net income here is the $489M available to common stockholders (after $17M of preferred dividends on total net income of $506M), matching the $2.31 diluted EPS.
